prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: Silent Storm game diffuse RGB565 UV texture atlas, 128x128 original, HD reconstruction.
Input image: the supplied image is the sole edit target; use it as an exact spatial template.
Primary request: Increase visible surface detail and edge clarity while preserving the original game art, at exactly 4x dimensions (512x512). Output only the flat square texture atlas, no product rendering.
Composition invariants: Preserve exact normalized UV positions. The round clock occupies ONLY the upper-left x=0..61 and y=0..64 area. Preserve the black unused region to its right and below; keep it black. Preserve the full-width horizontal housing surface strip at the bottom approximately y=88 through 127; keep every horizontal boundary exactly where it is. Do not enlarge the clock to fill the canvas, move islands, crop, rotate, add margins, or repack.
Materials: Preserve aged warm yellow/ivory clock dial, dark metal rim, thin black hands, the original dark numeral-like glyphs/tick marks, and the muted brown-gray housing material. Enhance only fine existing material detail: subtle grain, grime, edge wear. Preserve original pattern scale and all original color relationships and baked shading.
Constraints: Keep the exact number, arrangement and shape of marks, hands, panels, seams, cracks and holes. No new plaque, screw, bolt, logo, label, symbol, object, decorative border, or scene. Keep the original numeral glyphs exactly as visible. Do not replace ambiguous marks with guessed Roman or Arabic numbers. No raised dimensional typography; all dial marks remain flat paint. Keep original dark exposure; brightness will be matched programmatically. Fully opaque RGB texture with black unused regions; no alpha background.
Condition: This is the intact clock. Preserve intact dial and hands, their precise angles, the minute marks and all original subtle wear. Do not introduce damage or change the clock time.
CRITICAL ORIGINAL PRINT ORIENTATION: The Arabic digits 1 through 12 printed ring in the source is rotated as a whole by 180 degrees. Preserve this unusual original UV print orientation; do not correct it into a normal clock. At the TOP is the inverted 6, at the RIGHT is inverted 9, at the BOTTOM is inverted 12, and at the LEFT is inverted 3. Every other numeral follows the same whole-ring 180-degree turn: individual glyphs are upside down too. Clock hands keep their ORIGINAL image-space angles and are NOT rotated. Preserve the lower housing strip orientation and all damage/chip locations.
uv_registration_reason: Source is an opaque atlas with a face at (0,1)-(61,65), housing strip x=1..128 y=88..128 split at original horizontal seams y=99 and y=108, and otherwise black unused pixels. Raw clock and housing occupied bounds were independently inspected and are registered per island to correct generator margins without global repacking.
review_concern: Review inverted Arabic glyphs and original damaged versus intact hand directions.

prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: flat square Silent Storm diffuse texture UV atlas, HD reconstruction.
Input image: the sole edit target is a 4x nearest-enlarged source atlas. For preparation only, its clock face island was turned 180 degrees; the production importer will turn that island back. Match THIS supplied orientation exactly, including hands and damage.
Primary request: Reconstruct crisp faithful fine surface detail without changing the source forms. Output the same square atlas, not a 3D object render.
UV composition: clock face stays entirely in the upper-left x=0..244,y=4..260 part of a 512x512 equivalent canvas; housing stays in the lower x=4..512,y=352..512 horizontal strip. Black unused regions stay black, opaque. Do not crop, enlarge to fill, move, or repack.
Dial print: There are exactly twelve original flat black Roman numeral groups, I through XII. Preserve each group's count and shape: XII at top, III at right, VI at bottom, IX at left; I/II between top and right, IV/V between right and bottom, VII/VIII between bottom and left, X/XI between left and top. Follow original individual glyph orientations as shown. Preserve ticks; no extra numbers or symbols. All paint is flat, not raised typography.
Hands: Preserve precisely the two original hands in THIS input, long hand pointing left and the other hand upward-right. They must remain independent of numeral print and stay exactly at the original angles.
Materials: same aged warm yellow ivory painted dial, dark thin metal rim, thin dark metal hands, muted very dark gray-brown bottom housing. Add only fine material grain/edge wear at the original pattern scale. Keep original baked light and darkness; numerical brightness matching happens later.
Condition: Intact clock; preserve intact dial and subtle original wear without holes or cracks.
Avoid: new labels, plaques, bolt heads, screws, logos, objects, scene, extra hands, new holes, changed panels or seams, canvas border, halo, transparency. Preserve all horizontal housing divisions exactly.
uv_registration_reason: Source is an opaque atlas with a face at (0,1)-(61,65), housing strip x=1..128 y=88..128 split at original horizontal seams y=99 and y=108, and otherwise black unused pixels. Raw clock and housing occupied bounds were independently inspected and are registered per island to correct generator margins without global repacking. Clock edit target was explicitly rotated 180 degrees for generation; only clock crop is rotated back to restore original print/hand/damage UV orientation.
review_concern: Roman glyphs now have original sequence restored through helper and inverse rotation; inspect VIII group and dial paint orientation.
